pattern.name: NEGATIVE_CLAIM_REQUIRES_CLOSED_SEARCH_UNIVERSE
pattern.core: A non-detection inside search universe S may be promoted to an absence claim only within a scope for which coverage and detection sensitivity are adequate; otherwise preserve NOT_FOUND_WITHIN_S, UNKNOWN or UNRESOLVED.

classification.STRONG_SUPPORT: The source explicitly distinguishes non-detection from absence because search/source coverage is incomplete, non-authoritative, not exhaustive or sensitivity-limited; OR it explicitly requires exhaustive/authoritative/complete coverage before an absence claim may be admitted.
classification.WEAK_SUPPORT: The source preserves a scoped negative, UNKNOWN or UNRESOLVED result and separately records search/source limitations, but the dependency between limitation and negative-claim scope is implicit.
classification.CONTRADICTION: The source explicitly promotes a global absence claim from a search it simultaneously declares incomplete, non-authoritative, non-exhaustive or insufficiently sensitive, without another premise that closes the missing universe.
classification.NOT_APPLICABLE: The source does not contain a non-detection/search-universe relation relevant to absence inference. Generic OPEN/BLOCKED/negative results are insufficient.

coverage_toggle_control.precondition: Only STRONG_SUPPORT source families with an explicit coverage-sensitive rule may enter the destructive control.
coverage_toggle_control.failure_condition: Verdict is invariant to coverage state even though the source explicitly defines coverage as the boundary controlling admissible absence.
coverage_toggle_control.rule: Counterfactual branches must never be mislabeled as observed executions.
